clue.text: Accepted being sent back to find healthier hot drink?

indicators.note: sent back tells us to read the synonym for accepted from end to start

parts.note: to have faced something is to have accepted it

explanation.surface: Someone's suggestion, once accepted, is returned so they can find a better drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being sent back' turns FACED round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee without caffeine is thought to be kinder to health, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Final month with gold furnishings

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, ends the year
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A December makeover with gilded furnishings.
explanation.definitionFit: The furnishings and decoration of a room make up its interior styling.

clue.text: Camden's first bohemians get takeaway from these?

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word Camden's

parts.note: hippies are unconventional, free-living bohemians

explanation.surface: The arty types of Camden, a trendy north London district, buy their food to go.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIPPIES is British slang for fish-and-chip shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish-and-chip shops are where many Britons buy a hot meal to carry home.

clue.text: Crosses either side of Japan's top water features

indicators.note: the crossings sit on both sides, so they wrap around the letter from Japan

parts.note: fords are shallow river crossings; to ford is to cross

indicators.note: top picks out just the opening letter of Japan's

explanation.surface: Crossings flank Japan's best ornamental ponds and fountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either side of' puts FORDS round J.
explanation.definitionFit: Long sea inlets between cliffs are natural landmarks made of water, as in Norway.

clue.text: Cambridge is happy to exhibit eastern performer

indicators.note: to exhibit means to put on show, here letters found within the words Cambridge is happy

explanation.surface: Cambridge is pleased to put on show an artist from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese hostess trained to entertain with music and dance is a performer from the Far East.

clue.text: Scottish town beginning to organise prohibition

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of the word organise

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A Scottish town starts arranging a ban on something.
explanation.definitionFit: A port town on Scotland's west coast, known for its whisky distillery and ferries.

clue.text: Urge schoolmaster's top student?

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
the head is the headmaster of a school

explanation.surface: Pushing the headmaster's best pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly academic, brainy person is informally called this; a top student fits.

clue.text: Pitcher of beer for Spooner's dance

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds, after the Reverend Spooner who mixed them up

parts.note: bitter is a British style of draught beer
a jug is a pitcher

explanation.surface: A jug of beer is offered in exchange for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER JUG with its initial letters swapped becomes JITTER BUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively swing dance popular in 1940s America.

clue.text: Unfortunately, partner's tan is see-through

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone awry, so the letters of partner's tan are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sadly my partner's suntan shows through.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear like glass lets light pass so one can look straight through it.

clue.text: One in vehicle going to old African city

indicators.note: in says the numeral goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone drives off to an ancient African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' qualifies the letter O, not the city; Cairo is the capital of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian capital on the Nile is a major city of Africa.

clue.text: Some crabs in thick green liquid

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Crabs sitting in a thick green soup.
explanation.definitionFit: This strong anise-flavoured spirit is famously emerald-coloured, the 'green fairy'.

clue.text: Persuaded sculptor to box in gym

indicators.note: to box means to enclose, so the sculptor wraps round the gym letters

parts.note: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A sculptor is talked into boxing at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roped in is the idiom for being talked into joining something.

clue.text: Endurance refitting mast in Antarctica, primarily

indicators.note: refitting means putting together anew, so the letters of mast in are rearranged
primarily asks for the opening letter of Antarctica

explanation.surface: Repairing a ship's mast in Antarctica takes endurance, recalling Shackleton's ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refitting' rearranges MASTIN into STAMIN; then the A of Antarctica.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying power and endurance are synonyms for the ability to keep going.

clue.text: Cook an insect, for example

indicators.note: cook can mean falsify or rework, so the letters of an insect are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cooking an insect, say, as an exotic meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A case or example; we say 'for instance' just as we say 'for example'.

clue.text: Nobleman with decoration for body part

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour or decoration

explanation.surface: A decorated aristocrat with a part of his anatomy mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft lower part of the outer ear is a part of the body.

clue.text: Alfred leaves one country for another

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so those letters go out of the country's name

parts.note: Australia is a country
Al is short for Alfred

explanation.surface: Alfred emigrates from one country to another.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alpine nation is a second, different country from the first one named.

clue.text: Government cut short course of treatment

indicators.note: cut short says the final letter of that word is removed

parts.note: a regimen is a prescribed course of treatment

explanation.surface: The government curtails a medical programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a ruling system or government, often authoritarian.

clue.text: Go on with me up the pub: The King's Head

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word me is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: head means the opening letter of King's

explanation.surface: An invitation to head up to the King's Head, a common British pub name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ME to EM; K is the head of King's.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go on board a ship or begin a venture.

clue.text: What's demanded by one who lost sleep at church?

definitions.text: What's demanded by one who lost

parts.note: REM is the rapid-eye-movement stage of sleep

explanation.surface: A worshipper who dozed off in church wants another go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost sleep' tempts a reading about insomnia; 'lost' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeated side typically demands a second game to win back pride.

clue.text: Pay attention, holding cross that's cursed

indicators.note: holding means the attention word grips the cross inside it

parts.note: to heed is to pay attention
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: Take note of the cursed cross someone is holding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hexed has had a spell or jinx put on them.

clue.text: Angela's baked a pasta dish

indicators.note: baked means cooked, so the letters of Angela's are reworked

explanation.surface: Angela has cooked an Italian meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered sheets of pasta with sauce and cheese, oven-cooked.

clue.text: Island's small boat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
Noah's ark was a boat

explanation.surface: An island's little boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Channel Island near Guernsey, known for having no cars.

clue.text: Seize a former partner, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a phrase spoken out loud matches the entry

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, so this is the phrase an ex

explanation.surface: Grabbing a former lover, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: To take territory by force is to seize it, the verb sense of the entry.

clue.text: Weather forecaster that can take the pressure?

definitions.text: Weather forecaster that can take the pressure?

parts.words: Weather forecaster that can take the pressure?
parts.note: the instrument that reads atmospheric pressure is used to predict weather; take a reading, not cope with stress

explanation.walkthrough: 'take the pressure' suggests coping with stress; here it means measure air pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge of air pressure whose readings forecast fair or stormy weather.

clue.text: Work requirement, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken aloud to give the entry

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: A job requirement, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To work dough or muscles with the hands is to press and fold them.
